findings.title: You can't type a space in a gap's words box
findings.detail: The words box in GapChip is controlled by `gap.prompt`. That value comes from the composer's `animationTiming`, which is `timingFor(draft.frames.length, savedTiming, engine)` (composer.tsx:565). `timingFor` trims every gap's prompt (src/lib/inbetween.ts:138). So when someone types 'she ', the draft saves 'she ', the next render shows 'she', and the space is lost. The next letter makes 'shej'. Words with more than one word can only be pasted, never typed. I checked this with a scratch test: timingFor(3, {gaps:[{frames:33,speed:1,prompt:'she '},…]}).gaps[0].prompt === 'she'. tests/e2e/inbetweening.mjs did not catch it because Playwright's fill() sets the whole value at once.
findings.fix: Keep the untrimmed words in the draft and the box, and trim only when the request is built: in framesRequest/requestTiming, or in a timingFor option the UI path skips.

findings.title: Turning Animation off, or switching to another model, still sends extra.inbetween and extra.stillMouth to that model's API
findings.detail: setTiming and the Keep mouth still switch write params.extra.inbetween and params.extra.stillMouth into the draft. switchStyle(false) keeps d.params, extra included, and so does any later model pick. buildRequest sends draft.params as it is, and buildPayload copies every params.extra key into the API body (payload.ts:529). I checked this with a scratch test: a cloud Frames run on FLUX 3 Max (FRAMES_MODELS.cloud) whose draft still held them produced the fal body {…,"inbetween":{"gaps":[…],"fps":16},"stillMouth":true} for blackforestlabs/flux-3-max/keyframes-to-video. Endpoints that check their inputs strictly will refuse it, and the rest receive keys they don't know. On the open engine, Wan 2.2's chain happens to delete these keys (createKeyframeFilm), but a non-chained model or another studio model does not.
findings.fix: In switchStyle, and whenever the model changes away from an inbetween model, remove inbetween and stillMouth from params.extra. Or let buildRequest drop them unless model.options.inbetween is set. Add a test.

findings.title: The last keyframe of an animation is labelled 'Middle frame'
findings.detail: With animation on, the role is `i === 0 ? 'Start frame' : 'Middle frame'`, so the final keyframe, which the film ends on, shows 'Middle frame' visibly (line 285) and to screen readers. It should read 'End frame'.

findings.title: Assist/MCP drops playback_fps without a word when no gaps are given
findings.detail: animationOf only builds `inbetween` when gaps are present. A job with playback_fps: 16 and no gaps runs at the engine's default (24 on the GPU). Also, when the job carries no engine of its own and the context engine is cloud, keyframeTimes are computed at 24 fps. The server re-derives the timing from extra.inbetween, so the second point is cosmetic.

findings.title: Memory with long animations has no cap
findings.detail: One prompt holds every gap's decoded frames plus the batched copy. Ten keyframes at 81 frames and 720p is about 8 GB of float frames held twice, so roughly 16 GB+ of system RAM. The eval hardware note mentions that RAM grows with length, but nothing caps or warns in the UI. Leave it as is until a real GPU run, but keep it in mind.

fix.finalSummary: Fuobe Animation (keyframe in-betweening) is finished on o/inbetweening.
